product.name: slot
promise: One pool of build slots for every build on a machine.
Builds queue instead of oversubscribing the CPU.
product.lede: When several coding-agent sessions share one workstation, every cargo test and go test sizes itself to the whole machine, and a dozen of them run at once. slot runs every build through one daemon that owns a GNU-make jobserver: cargo and rustc draw their parallelism from one token pool, a go job holds a fixed share, anything else holds one slot. A build that has to wait is queued. Output and exit code are those of the command.
product.description: Run every cargo, go and make build on a machine through one shared GNU-make jobserver pool, with a queue, a live web view and an optional remote build server.
product.meta: One Rust binary · Linux x86_64 and aarch64 · Apache-2.0

sections.title: Prefix, queue, run, return.
sections.lede: The client is the same binary as the daemon. Prefixing a command with slot is the only change to how it is called.

steps.label: prefix
steps.title: Send the command
steps.description: slot cargo test sends the command, its directory and its environment to the daemon over a unix socket.

steps.label: queue
steps.title: Wait for slots
steps.description: The daemon picks the toolchain from the command name and queues the job by its priority until the slots it needs are free.

steps.label: run
steps.title: Share one pool
steps.description: The job starts with the jobserver in MAKEFLAGS and CARGO_MAKEFLAGS; cargo and rustc take more tokens from the same pool as they parallelise.

steps.label: return
steps.title: Same output, same exit code
steps.description: stdout and stderr stream back to the caller, the exit code is passed through, and the job log records the run.

sections.title: Two jobs on a pool of four slots.
sections.lede: A go job holds all four slots. A second job queues, runs when a slot is free, and keeps its exit code.

sections.title: One scheduler instead of flock files and -j flags.
sections.lede: Sessions that cannot see each other stop guessing how many cores are free.

items.title: cargo and rustc on one jobserver
items.description: cargo holds one slot and draws more from the shared FIFO, so all Rust builds together stay within the pool.

items.title: go with a fixed share
items.description: A go job holds four slots by default and runs with -p set to what it holds.

items.title: Wrappers pass the pool down
items.description: slot task check holds one slot; cargo started inside the task shares the same pool.

items.title: Live web view
items.description: Every queued and running job with its level, slot usage, cores per toolchain, live output and each project's share of the pool on 127.0.0.1:7411.

items.title: Headroom for your desktop
items.description: slot headroom 40 or one slider keeps 40 % of the CPU out of builds; with --base machine it counts the load outside the pool too. While a call uses the microphone or camera, the daemon raises it to the call value and puts the old value back 2 minutes after.

items.title: Waits for disk and memory
items.description: A job queues while its filesystem has under 25 GB free or memory would run short, and slot status says why.

items.title: Claude Code plugin
items.description: A hook refuses a build an agent starts outside the pool and names the slot command to run instead; the warden lists sessions that still build outside it.

items.title: Remote build server
items.description: Set SLOT_HOST and builds run on another machine; the repository is synced with rsync and target directories stay there.

items.title: Runs anyway
items.description: When the daemon cannot be reached, the command runs locally and slot prints one line saying so.

sections.title: What exists and what does not.
sections.lede: Shipped means in the code and covered by tests. Planned means not built.
